approach: Extend the published CKgP / plane-quartic presentation from n≤11 to the missing pointed case M_3,12 by stratifying the n=12 independent-conditions wall, then feed pure-weight algebraicity into the degree-16 low-homology induction.
assumptions: Q-coefficients throughout, as in the packet scope.
Working on the moduli stack M_{g,n}, not its coarse space (mandatory scope trap).
SRC-0004 Theorems 6.1–6.2 apply at the endpoint n=2g+6=12 for g=3, so Hyp_{3,12} is available as a CKgP stratum.

The weight/duality identification used in SRC-0002 §6.2 to pass from algebraicity of pure cohomology of the open M to the pure BM quotient W_{-k} H^{BM}_k(M) continues to apply at (g,n,k)=(3,12,16) without new correction terms.
For Claim K: the incidence stack I is taken over the locus where C∩Q is reduced of length 12; non-reduced or non-transverse intersections are treated as a deeper closed stratum (not yet constructed).
claims: ## Setup and why (g,n)=(3,12) is forced at degree 16

Claim A (reduction range). By SRC-0002, equation (6.1), there is a right-exact sequence H_k(∂̂ Mbar_{g,n}) → H_k(Mbar_{g,n}) → W_{-k} H^{BM}_k(M_{g,n}) → 0. Combined with the BM-vanishing ranges of [CLP23, Prop. 2.1] (packet THM-0004), for even k=16 and n≥2 the open pure-weight input is needed precisely when 16 ≥ 2g−2+n, i.e. n ≤ 2g+14−12 wait: n ≤ 16−2g+2. For g=3 this is n≤12. Thus (3,12) is the maximal marking number forced in genus 3.

Claim B (published CKgP wall). SRC-0002 Table 1 and SRC-0004 Corollary 7.5 give c(3)=11: M_{3,n} has CKgP and A_*=R_* for all n≤11. Packet THM-0005 records this bound. Hence the degree-16 induction discharges all genus-3 base cases except M_3,12.

Claim C (what CKgP buys). SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3: if a smooth open X ⊂ Xbar (Xbar smooth proper DM) has CKgP, then cl: ⊕ A^i(X) → ⊕ W_k H^k(X) is surjective, so for even k the pure piece W_k H^k(X) is pure Hodge–Tate (algebraic). Proposition 4.5 packages the same input as W_k H^k(M_{g,n})=RH^k for n≤c(g), which is exactly what the low-homology induction uses to make W_{-k} H^{BM}_k tautological/Tate.
## Geometry of the published n≤11 argument

Claim D (excision into hyperelliptic + plane quartics). For g=3, SRC-0004 Corollary 7.5 proceeds by excision: (i) Hyp_{3,n} has CKgP and supports only tautological classes for n≤2g+6=12 (Theorems 6.1–6.2), and (ii) M_{3,n}\Hyp_{3,n} ≅ F_{4,n}, the stack of smooth n-pointed plane quartics. The μ_3-gerbe G_{4,n}→F_{4,n} preserves CKgP and rational Chow.

Claim E (independent-conditions presentation). SRC-0004 Lemmas 7.1–7.2 construct G_{d,n} for n≤3d−1 as an open inside a tower of projective bundles over BSL_3 (evaluation of degree-d forms at the n points is surjective on that range). For d=4 this is n≤11. Lemma 7.4 then identifies the Chern generators with λ- and ψ-classes, so A_*=R_* on the non-hyperelliptic open.

Claim F (sharpness of n≤11). In the proof of Lemma 7.1 the residual line bundle O_{P^2}(−d)|_C ⊗ ω_C(Γ) has degree −3d+n. For d=4 this is n−12. For n≤11 the degree is negative, so H^0=0 and evaluation is surjective. At n=12 the residual has degree 0, so evaluation can fail.

Claim G (hyperelliptic stratum at n=12 is already covered). For g=3, the bound n≤2g+6 of SRC-0004 Theorems 6.1–6.2 is exactly n≤12. Thus Hyp_{3,12} has CKgP and A_* generated by ψ-classes (and the irreducible nodal hyperelliptic boundary class on the partial compactification I_{3,12}). Excision therefore reduces CKgP of M_{3,12} to CKgP of the non-hyperelliptic open U_nh := M_{3,12}\Hyp_{3,12}.

Claim H (stratify U_nh by independence of markings). Let d=4. Write Ev: W_4 → ⊕_{i=1}^{12} O(4)|_{p_i} for the evaluation of quartics at the twelve marked points on the universal P^2-bundle over BSL_3. Let U_ind ⊂ (PV)^{12} be the open where Ev is surjective, and let G_ind := G_{4,12} ∩ P(K)|_{U_ind} be the corresponding open of smooth pointed plane quartics with independent markings. The same tower argument as Lemma 7.2 shows G_ind has CKgP (open in a projective-bundle tower over BSL_3). The image N ⊂ U_nh of G_ind is therefore a CKgP open in U_nh.

Claim I (dependent locus). Let D := U_nh \ N be the closed locus of non-hyperelliptic (C;p_1,…,p_12) for which the twelve points impose dependent conditions on |O_{P^2}(4)|. By the degree-0 residual computation of Claim F, for a smooth plane quartic C one has O_C(1)≅ω_C and the residual is O_C(Γ−3). Hence H^0(residual)≠0 iff O_C(Γ)≅O_C(3), i.e. the divisor of marked points is a cubic section of C. Thus D is the locus of smooth pointed plane quartics whose markings are cut by a cubic.

Claim J (incidence presentation of D, conditional). Let I be the stack over BSL_3 of triples (C,Q,(p_i)) where C is a smooth plane quartic, Q is a cubic with no common component with C, and (p_1,…,p_12) is an ordering of the scheme-theoretic intersection C∩Q (assumed reduced of length 12). Then I sits openly in a product of projective bundles P(Sym^4 V^∨)×_{BSL_3} P(Sym^3 V^∨) with a finite étale ordering cover of the transverse locus, hence I has CKgP by the standard projective-bundle and open-embedding lemmas (SRC-0004 Lemmas 3.3, 3.7; SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2). The forgetful map φ: I → D, (C,Q,(p_i))↦(C;(p_i)), is a candidate proper surjection.

Claim K (uniqueness of the cubic, geometric points). On a non-hyperelliptic genus-3 curve, H^0(O_{P^2}(3))→H^0(O_C(3)) is an isomorphism (kernel H^0(O(−1))=0; both sides have dimension 10). Therefore a divisor Γ with O_C(Γ)≅O_C(3) is cut by a unique cubic up to scale. So φ is bijective on geometric points of the reduced transverse locus. If φ is proper and surjective as a morphism of stacks (or a finite gerbe), then SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(2) would give CKgP for D.

Claim L (excision synthesis, conditional). If Claims H and K are established as morphisms of stacks with the stated properties, then U_nh = N ∪ D is a two-stratum CKgP stratification, and with Claim G one obtains CKgP for M_{3,12}. Lemma 4.3 then yields that every pure piece W_k H^k(M_{3,12}) is algebraic, hence pure Hodge–Tate for even k. In particular the pure-weight BM quotient W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12}) needed by (6.1) would be pure Tate (a direct sum of Q(8) after the standard duality/weight identification used in SRC-0002 §6.2).

Claim M (scope relative to RED-0001). Even a complete proof of CKgP for M_{3,12} discharges only one of the five residual pure-weight inputs listed in RED-0001 (M_3,12; M_5,8; M_6,6; M_7,4; M_8,n for n=0,1,2). The other four cases require separate gonality/Hurwitz or Mukai-type extensions beyond published c(g) bounds and are not treated here.

Claim N (what is not claimed). This attempt does not claim: (i) that H^{16}(Mbar_{g,n}) is pure Tate for all (g,n); (ii) that A_*(M_{3,12})=R_*(M_{3,12}) in full (only the pure-weight / CKgP consequence is targeted for the induction); (iii) any conclusion from Chenevier–Lannes arithmetic predictions, from semisimplifications of Galois representations, or from an unproved perfectness of a tautological pairing.
gap_markers: GAP-1 (stacky properness of φ: I→D). Uniqueness of the cubic on geometric points does not by itself prove that φ is a proper surjective representable morphism (or finite gerbe) of algebraic stacks. One must construct I rigorously as a DM stack, check valuative properness when markings collide or C acquires singularities in the limit, and identify stabilizers. Until this is done, Prop. 4.2(2) cannot be applied to D.

GAP-2 (non-transverse / non-reduced cubic sections). Claim I identifies D set-theoretically with cubic sections, but the dependent locus may contain deeper strata where Ev has corank ≥2, or where C∩Q is non-reduced (shared tangent directions, flexes, etc.). These strata need a separate CKgP presentation; they are not covered by the transverse incidence stack I.

GAP-3 (Chow generators on D, optional for pure Tate but needed for tautological generation). Even if D has CKgP, Lemma 4.3 only gives algebraicity of pure weight cohomology, not A_*=R_*. Extending Lemma 7.4 (λ/ψ generation) across the dependent locus requires a separate computation of A_*(D). The degree-16 induction only needs pure Tate of the BM pure-weight quotient, so full tautological generation is stronger than required — but it is not proved here either.

GAP-4 (duality bookkeeping for W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}). Packet THM-0003 / SRC-0002 (6.1) identifies the inductive quotient with W_{-k} H^{BM}_k(M). Passing from 'W_k H^k(M) is pure Tate' (Lemma 4.3) to 'W_{-k} H^{BM}_k(M) is pure Tate' uses Poincaré duality / weight conventions for the open stack of dimension d_{3,12}=18. This identification is standard in the published k≤14 argument but is not re-derived here line-by-line for the new base case; a fully rigorous writeup must track Tate twists and BM vs. compactly supported gradeds explicitly.

GAP-5 (no CKgP proof completed). Claims H–L form a strategy, not a finished proof. The published literature stops at n≤11 for g=3 (c(3)=11). This attempt does not close GAP-1 or GAP-2, so CKgP for M_{3,12} remains unproved.

GAP-6 (RED-0001 is not reduced to a theorem). Remaining open pure-weight inputs M_5,8, M_6,6, M_7,4, M_8,n (n=0,1,2) are untouched. Genus 0,1,2 and n≤c(g) cases for g≤7 are already covered by THM-0005–0007 and do not remove these.

GAP-7 (forbidden completeness shortcuts, explicitly declined). One must not deduce pure Tate of H^{16}(Mbar_{3,12}) from: Chenevier–Lannes conductor-1 predictions; Bergström–Faber point-count tables conditional on those predictions; semisimplification of ℓ-adic representations; or an admcycles pairing RH^8 × RH_8 → Q whose perfectness is not proved. None of those routes is used, and none is available as a substitute for GAP-1–GAP-5.
